SMTO-GWT-0071 — A GPU reset may not have finished cleanly

GUID: a59fd118-96d8-59eb-aa31-70247ba7e090
Slug: gpu-reset-failed
Domain: GWT · Subsystem: gpu

What happened

  • SMTO recorded that this graphics card didn't come back as expected after a reset. That doesn't prove the card is broken, but its current state hasn't been checked yet.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In the conversation, ask SMTO to show the GPU status and list the GPUs on that computer. If the card appears with normal readings, it came back after the reset and nothing more is needed.
  2. Don't ask SMTO to reset the GPU again just to see what happens. A second reset can't show what the first one did, and it could interrupt programs now using the card.
  3. If the card is missing or shows no readings, ask the person who manages that computer to check it with their own recovery steps. A card that doesn't come back needs hands-on attention on that computer, which SMTO can't provide.

What success looks like

  • The GPU appears in the device list with current readings, without another reset.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the computer with the GPU. Don't reset or restart the card again until they have looked at it.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A GPU reset-recovery failure was recorded for this device (legacy kind gpu.reset_failed; current code reports uncertain reset outcomes as gpu.operation_outcome_unknown), so the reset's effect and the device's health are not established.

What this means

  • The catalog retains a reset-recovery failure identity, but no current direct branch emits it; current uncertain reset recovery is reported through operation_outcome_unknown. This compatibility definition has no direct current producer; it cannot establish the duration, success or physical consequences of a reset.

Why this can happen

  • The catalog retains a reset-recovery failure identity, but no current direct branch emits it; current uncertain reset recovery is reported through operation_outcome_unknown.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the retained reset attempt and exact UUID's current health; do not invent a recovery deadline or hardware cause from this compatibility label.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the original reset receipt and the Gateway job record for that execution, then read gpu.devices and gpu.device for the exact UUID to establish current health. Do not replay the reset; if the device is absent or unhealthy, follow the host operator's NVIDIA recovery procedure.
  • Inspect the original reset receipt and exact device health; use the owning operator's recovery procedure if health remains unresolved.

Retry and execution caution

  • For a mutation, inspect the exact UUID and resolve any active execution or uncertain effect before issuing a new operation. Never replay a reset or an unobservable clock change to infer its result.

How to verify the fix

  • The original reset outcome and current device health are established without automatically repeating reset.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations, kill GPU clients automatically or invent sensor values.

Technical notes

  • This compatibility definition has no direct current producer; it cannot establish the duration, success or physical consequences of a reset.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
